title: 3D Atherogenesis-on-Chip Model for Endothelial-Macrophage Crosstalk Study
author: Hanford, Dzobo, et al.
materials: The secretome of the cells in the chips was measured using the Proteome Profiler Human XL Cytokine Array Kit on digested collagen. The digested collagen was diluted 5x in Array Buffer 6. Upon imaging on a Bio-Rad ChemiDoc system, the exposure was initially set to take one image each minute between 1 and 10 min. Following this, the exposure time was set to 20 min, and the image created was used for further analysis.

steps.title: Prepare endothelial growth medium
steps.instruction: Add the complete EGM‑2 bullet kit to endothelial basal medium (EBM‑2) as described in the Materials and Equipment section.

steps.title: Activate and coat chips
steps.instruction: Perform chip activation, washing, fibronectin coating, and pre‑incubation while avoiding bubbles.

substeps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet (BSC) align all chips facing the same direction in a 150 mm dish and label each carrier with a permanent marker.
Turn off the BSC light (activation solution is light‑sensitive).
Prepare activation solution: mix 1 vial ER‑1 powder with 10 mL ER‑2 solution (final 0.5 mg/mL). Use immediately.
Pipette activation solution into both inlets of each chip (≈200 µL fills ~3 chips); aspirate any spill‑over from outlets with a tissue.
Place chips in a UV light box for 10 min.
Wash chips twice with ER‑2 solution, then repeat the activation‑solution pipetting and UV‑10‑min step.
After the second UV activation, wash each channel twice with ER‑2 solution and once with cold PBS.
Aspirate cold PBS from the bottom (vascular) channel only, leaving PBS in the top (gel) channel.
Add 1.5 mL PBS to the cap of a 15 mL conical tube and place the tube in the 150 mm dish to provide humidity.
Prepare fibronectin (FN) at 30 µg/mL.
Fully aspirate PBS from the bottom channel, keep PBS in the top channel.
Introduce 50 µL FN solution through the bottom channel inlet until a small droplet forms at the outlet.
Add a droplet of FN above both inlet and outlet ports of the bottom channel and a droplet of PBS to the inlet and outlet of the top channel.
Inspect channels under a microscope; if bubbles are present, flush with FN solution until cleared.
Place the dish with chips (and the PBS‑filled tube) in the incubator (37 °C, 5 % CO₂) for 1 h before cell seeding.
Activated, FN‑coated chips can be stored at 4 °C in sterile PBS for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Isolate CD14+ monocytes
steps.instruction: Perform density‑gradient isolation and magnetic bead selection to obtain CD14+ monocytes from donor blood.

substeps.instruction: Collect 2 × 10 mL EDTA‑treated blood from an informed‑consent donor.
Add 15 mL Lymphoprep to two 50 mL Leucosep tubes.
Spin at 1000 g for 30 s at 21 °C (maximum brake).
Distribute blood over two 50 mL Falcon tubes; rinse empty blood tubes twice with 4 mL PBS‑EDTA and add residual blood to the Falcon tubes.
Dilute blood with PBS‑EDTA to a final volume of 35 mL.
Add the 35 mL diluted blood to each Leucosep tube containing Lymphoprep.
Balance tubes and centrifuge at 1000 g for 15 min (acceleration 9, deceleration 1) at 21 °C without brake.
Carefully remove ~15 mL plasma layer with a 10 mL pipette.
Pour PBMC layer into new 50 mL Falcon tubes (one tube per original tube).
Adjust volume to 50 mL with cold PBS‑EDTA (work on ice from now on).
Spin at 300 g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Remove supernatant (vacuum or decant).
Resuspend cell pellets, pool into one 50 mL Falcon tube, and wash with cold PBS‑EDTA up to 50 mL.
Count cells.
Spin again at 300 g for 10 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant with a P1000.
Resuspend cells in 40 µL MACS buffer per 10 × 10⁶ cells.
Add 10 µL CD14 magnetic beads per 10 × 10⁶ cells; mix and incubate 15 min on ice (2–8 °C).
Wash by adding 1 mL MACS buffer per 10 × 10⁶ cells; spin 300 g for 10 min at 4 °C; aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend up to 100 × 10⁶ cells in 500 µL MACS buffer.
Place an MS column in a magnetic separator (keep plunger sterile) and rinse with 500 µL MACS buffer.
Apply the 500 µL cell suspension to the column reservoir; wash column three times with 500 µL MACS buffer (add buffer only after reservoir is empty).
Remove column from separator, place on a 15 mL collection tube.
Flush 1 mL MACS buffer through the column reservoir while pushing the plunger to elute magnetically labeled cells.
Spin eluate at 300 g for 10 min at 4 °C; resuspend cells in 1–3 mL RPMI‑GlutaMAX.
Count cells and resuspend monocytes to 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL in RPMI‑GlutaMAX.

steps.title: Prepare collagen‑monocyte gel
steps.instruction: Make a 3 mg/mL neutralized collagen mixture on ice and combine with monocytes.

substeps.instruction: Keep all equipment (tips, racks, tubes) on ice; use frozen tips.
Mix collagen with RPMI to achieve a final collagen concentration of 3 mg/mL.
Neutralize the collagen by adding 4 µL 1 N NaOH; adjust pH to ~8.0, adding 1 µL increments if needed.
On ice, combine equal volumes of neutralized collagen and the monocyte suspension prepared above.

steps.title: Equilibrate media for Zoë
steps.instruction: Warm EGM‑2 and remove bubbles before use in the Zoë module.

substeps.instruction: Warm at least 4.5 mL EGM‑2 per chip in a 50 mL conical tube at 37 °C (water or bead bath) for ≥1 h.
Connect the tube to a Steriflip unit and apply vacuum to remove bubbles.
Leave the filtered medium under vacuum, then place the tube (cap loose) in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Prime Zoë pods
steps.instruction: Load media into pod reservoirs and run the prime cycle.

substeps.instruction: In the BSC, place Pods into the Zoë trays.
Add 1 mL pre‑equilibrated media to the Pod outlet reservoir for the top gel channel (to keep gel hydrated).
Pipette 3 mL pre‑equilibrated warm media into the inlet reservoir for the bottom (vascular) channel.
Add 500 µL pre‑equilibrated warm media to the outlet reservoir of the bottom channel (directly over the outlet via).
Insert the trays with Pods into the Zoë instrument and run the Prime cycle twice.
Inspect the underside of each Pod; small droplets should be visible at the ports where media were added. Re‑run Prime on any Pod lacking droplets.
Place a 4 mm diameter, 50 µm thick PET disc onto the inlet of the gel‑filled channel using tweezers; center it over the inlet port.

steps.title: Wash chips and place PET disc
steps.instruction: Perform a gravity wash of the bottom channel, add droplets to ports, and secure the PET disc.

substeps.instruction: In the BSC, remove all pipette tips from the chips.
Gravity‑wash the bottom channel only; if bubbles appear, flush with equilibrated media until cleared.
Add droplets of media to all four ports (inlet and outlet of both channels).
Place the 4 mm PET disc onto the gel‑channel inlet, depress firmly, and aspirate excess media next to the inlet port (do not remove droplets from outlet ports).

steps.title: Connect chips to pods
steps.instruction: Seat each chip carrier in its Pod and transfer to the Zoë.

substeps.instruction: Slide the chip carrier into the tracks on the underside of the Pod until fully seated.
Gently depress the chip tab to engage with the Pod.
Aspirate any excess medium from the chip surface visible through the Pod window; ensure the PET disc remains in place.
Place the Pod (with connected chip) onto the tray, verify sufficient media in inlet and outlet reservoirs, and ensure Pod lids are flat and secure.
Immediately place the trays with Pods and chips into the Zoë to maintain media temperature and gas equilibration.

steps.title: Program Zoë and run Regulate cycles
steps.instruction: Set flow parameters, run the Regulate cycle, flush vias, and repeat.

substeps.instruction: Program the Organ‑Chip culture conditions: gel‑filled channel flow rate = 0 µL/h; perfusion (vascular) channel flow rate = 10 µL/h; no mechanical stretch.
Run the Regulate cycle for 2 h.
After completion, flush the pod vias of the bottom channel by pipetting 200 µL pre‑equilibrated media directly over each via to dislodge bubbles.
Run a second Regulate cycle (can be performed the next day).

steps.title: Fix chips for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Fix cells with formaldehyde and perform extensive PBS washes.

substeps.instruction: Label all chips and arrange them in petri dishes.
Remove the PET disc from the gel‑channel inlet.
Plug both top and bottom outlets and the gel‑channel inlet with 200 µL non‑filtered tips.
Using a 200 µL tip, aspirate 200 µL of 3.7 % formaldehyde and slowly dispense into the bottom channel until ~½ of the volume is delivered; allow gravity flow into the top channel.
Add an additional 200 µL of 3.7 % formaldehyde to the inlet tip, bringing the total volume to 400 µL.
Incubate ≥1 h at room temperature (18–21 °C) on a rocker (fluid circulates between ports).
While still on the rocker, replace tips in all ports with fresh 200 µL tips.
Wash by adding 200 µL PBS to the bottom channel (tip remains in inlet, solution flows to top channel); wait 10 min.
Repeat PBS wash two more times (total three washes, each followed by 10 min incubation).
Store chips at 4 °C (protected from drying) for up to 2 weeks before proceeding.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Treat cells with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS.
Add 100 µL permeabilization solution to the inlet of the endothelial (bottom) channel; leave tip in place.
Incubate 30 min at room temperature (18–21 °C) on the rocker.
Remove tip and wash the channel three times with 200 µL PBS as described in the fixation wash steps.

steps.title: Block nonspecific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate chips with 5 % BSA in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL 5 % BSA in PBS to the inlet of the endothelial channel; keep tip inserted.
Incubate ≥1 h at room temperature (18–21 °C) on the rocker.
Remove tip and wash the channel three times with 200 µL PBS (same procedure as before).

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Apply primary antibodies diluted in 1 % BSA‑PBS to the endothelial channel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare each primary antibody in 1 % BSA‑PBS according to Table 1 (e.g., VE‑Cadherin 1:100, CD64 1:100, CD68 1:100, Hoechst 1:1000).
Add 100 µL of the appropriate primary antibody solution to the inlet of the endothelial channel; leave tip inserted.
Incubate 4 h at room temperature (18–21 °C) on the rocker.
Remove tip and wash the channel three times with 200 µL PBS.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add secondary antibodies in 1 % BSA‑PBS and incubate overnight.

substeps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibodies in 1 % BSA‑PBS as listed in Table 1 (e.g., Goat anti‑Mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 647 1:200, etc.).
Add 100 µL secondary antibody solution to the inlet of the endothelial channel; keep tip inserted.
Incubate overnight (≥12 h) at 4 °C on the rocker, protected from light.
Remove tip and wash the channel three times with 200 µL PBS.

steps.title: Nuclear staining
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei with Hoechst and store chips in the dark.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Hoechst (1:1000 dilution) to the inlet of the endothelial channel; keep tip inserted.
Incubate 4 h at room temperature (18–21 °C) in the dark.
Remove tip and wash the channel three times with 200 µL PBS.
Store chips in the dark at 4 °C; do not let them dry out. Image within 2 weeks.

steps.title: Harvest endothelial cells for RNA
steps.instruction: Collect cells from the bottom channel, lyse, and store for RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the bottom channel once with 200 µL PBS (pipette in through inlet, aspirate outflow).
Remove the PET disc from the gel‑channel inlet.
Plug the inlet and outlet of the top channel with empty 200 µL tips (to protect them).
Wash the bottom channel again with 200 µL PBS; aspirate completely, leaving the channel dry.
Plug the bottom‑channel outlet with an empty 200 µL tip (do not push tip fully against the channel).
Add 150 µL Accutase to the bottom channel inlet using a 200 µL tip; pipette up/down several times.
Incubate 4–5 min at room temperature in the BSC (or 2–3 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂).
Confirm cell detachment under a microscope; pipette up/down again to ensure complete detachment.
Collect the cell suspension into an RNase‑free Eppendorf tube.
Wash remaining cells by adding 150 µL RPMI‑GlutaMAX, pipette up/down, and collect the wash into the same tube.
Add 500 µL EGM‑2 to neutralize Accutase.
Spin at 400 g for 5 min at 21 °C.
Aspirate supernatant (pellet will be very small).
Resuspend pellet in 300 µL TRIzol (or store pellet at –70 °C until RNA isolation).
Proceed with your standard RNA isolation protocol; store lysate at –70 °C if not processed immediately.

steps.title: Digest collagen and collect macrophages
steps.instruction: Enzymatically digest the gel compartment and retrieve macrophages for RNA or flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Warm digestion solution (recipe in Materials) to 37 °C; 200 µL per chip is required.
Remove the PET disc from the gel‑channel inlet.
Plug the inlet and outlet of the top (gel) channel with pipette tips containing 50 µL digestion solution each.
Plug the bottom‑channel outlet with an empty tip; plug the bottom‑channel inlet with a tip containing 100 µL digestion solution.
Incubate the chip at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 1 h.
Pipette the digestion solution up/down in both channels (tips remain in place) to loosen the gel.
Incubate an additional 45 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Pipette up/down again to further break the gel.
If clumps remain, incubate an extra 30 min and repeat pipetting.
=== For RNA ===
Collect the collagen/cell mixture into an RNase‑free tube; rinse channels with PBS.
Spin at 500 g for 5 min at 21 °C; aspirate PBS.
Add 300 µL TRIzol, resuspend pellet, and store at –70 °C or proceed with RNA isolation.
=== For flow cytometry ===
Collect the digestion volume into a V‑ or U‑well 96‑well plate.
Add 150 µL cold FACS buffer, rinse both channels, and transfer to a second well.
Inspect under a microscope; repeat rinse if cells remain.
Repeat for all chips.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 g for 4 min at 4 °C; aspirate supernatant carefully.
Wash the cell pellet with 150 µL FACS buffer and centrifuge again (400 g, 4 min, 4 °C).
Proceed with your regular FACS staining protocol.

steps.title: Flow cytometry staining and acquisition
steps.instruction: Stain macrophages with the antibody panel and acquire data on a FACS Canto II.

substeps.instruction: Prepare antibody dilutions as listed in Table 2 (e.g., CD14‑APC‑H7 1:100, HLA‑DR‑PerCP‑Cy5.5 1:200, etc.).
Stain cells according to your standard FACS protocol.
Run samples on a FACS Canto II (laser settings as in Table 3).
Apply the gating strategy: FSC‑A vs SSC‑A → FSC‑H (singlets) → DAPI‑ (live) → individual macrophage markers.
Analyze marker expression; report percentages as described.

steps.title: Prepare and image cytokine array
steps.instruction: Process digested collagen for cytokine profiling and capture images on a ChemiDoc system.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the digested collagen 5‑fold in Array Buffer 6.
Apply the diluted sample to the Proteome Profiler Human XL Cytokine Array Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Image the membrane on a Bio‑Rad ChemiDoc: first acquire one image each minute from minute 1 to minute 10, then acquire a single 20‑minute exposure image for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze cytokine array data
steps.instruction: Quantify spot intensities, generate heat maps, and perform statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Use the DotBlot_Analysis.ijm12 macro in ImageJ to obtain mean spot pixel densities.
Calculate the proportion of each cytokine: unstimulated / (unstimulated + IL‑1β) and vice‑versa.
Plot proportional values as a heat map; plot absolute densities as bar graphs.
Perform statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism: unpaired two‑tailed t‑test for two‑group comparisons; one‑way ANOVA with multiple comparisons for three or more groups.
